title: Grateful Dead Live at Capitol Theater on 1970-11-05
lineage: Sony TC-110 with built-in microphone > MC > Cass >DAT > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Rough audience‑tape quality can't dim the brilliance of this 1970 show – a spacey Dark Star, fiery Other One and killer Not Fade Away sequence steal the spotlight.
ai_review.review: The performance is widely praised for its cosmic Dark Star, high‑energy Other One and tight Not Fade Away→Goin' Down The Road→Not Fade Away jam, with Garcia’s blues‑y guitar work and Phil’s rumbling bass highlighted.  However, listeners repeatedly note the AUD recording suffers from hiss, muffled mids and a distorted low end that makes it hard to enjoy without EQ tricks.  Overall fans love the show but are divided on its listenability.

ai_rating.rationale: Show quality scores cluster around 5 stars (excellent performance), while recording quality is consistently rated poor‑to‑fair, pulling the weighted average down to the high‑mid range.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Heavy hiss and tape grain, bass overly distorted/rumbly, mids muffled; occasional cuts in Not Fade Away sequence.  Listeners report needing EQ (reduce bass, add high‑end) to make it tolerable.

standout_songs: Not Fade Away → Goin' Down The Road → Not Fade Away
Lovelight (noted as less energized but still strong)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Shows a classic late‑1970 arc: Pigpen opener, high‑octane Other One into a deep‑space Dark Star, followed by the explosive Not Fade Away jam and a fiery St. Stephen, giving the night a cohesive, space‑filled momentum.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia delivers bluesy, Coltrane‑like riffs; top form on guitar throughout especially during Dark Star and Not Fade.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass described as rumbly, funky and rolling blues bottom runs; some reviewers suggest turning the bass down for comfort.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir (Bobby) noted for crisp rhythm chops that “stop them on a dime” during transitions.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith piano mentioned in Dark Star; Ned Lagin appears on keys for Other One/Dark Star but is barely audible.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey Hart’s absence noted; drum work generally praised but no specific criticism.
